(CNN) -- After deliberating for more than four hours, a jury convicted a Nevada man of 22 counts Tuesday for videotaping himself sexually assaulting a toddler, CNN affiliates report. Chester Arthur Stiles has been convicted of videtaping a sexual assault on a child. Chester Arthur Stiles, 38, faces a maximum sentence of life in prison. He was convicted of lewdness with a child, sexual assault with a minor, attempted sexual assault with a minor and other related charges. He showed no reaction as the verdict was read after more than four hours of jury deliberations, according to KLAS. Sentencing was set for May 8. The crime triggered a national manhunt and search for the girl when the tape surfaced in 2007. Jurors in Stiles' trial viewed the videotape, but the judge would not allow members sitting in the gallery to view it, and a screen was put up to block the jury box, said Michael Sommermeyer, spokesman for Clark County, Nevada, courts. Some members of the media were allowed to view the tape as well, but the judge did not want the reactions of reporters or the public to influence jurors, he said. The charges also related to another girl who Stiles was accused of sexually assaulting on videotape. The tape was given to authorities in September 2007 by a man who said he had found it in the desert five months before. On it, police found images of the small girl being sexually assaulted. After attempting unsuccessfully to find out the girl's identity, authorities turned to the media for help and released a picture of the girl, and the case drew nationwide attention. She was found in October 2007. An attorney for her mother said she was 7 years old and safe and healthy. The rape occurred before the girl's third birthday, while she was in the care of a baby-sitter her mother had hired, he said. The mother did not know the girl had been victimized. After the girl was found, authorities asked CNN and other news organizations to stop showing her picture. In an appearance on "The Dr. Phil Show," the girl's mother said the girl has no recollection of the assault. Stiles, a resident of Pahrump, Nevada, was arrested in a traffic stop in October 2007. Police said at the time they pulled Stiles' car over because it had no license plate, and became suspicious when the driver displayed an expired California license with a photo that did not match his appearance. Stiles eventually admitted who he was and that he was being sought, authorities said. The man who turned the tape over to authorities, Darrin Tuck, faced criminal charges because of the delay in turning it over, during which authorities alleged he showed it to others. A judge gave Tuck a one-year suspended sentence and three years of probation in April after he pleaded guilty to conspiracy to obstruct a public officer, according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal. He initially had faced a felony count of possession of child pornography.

# Nevada Man Convicted on 22 Counts for Videotaped Sexual Assault of Toddler

(CNN) -- Following more than four hours of deliberation, a jury on Tuesday convicted a Nevada man on 22 counts related to videotaping himself sexually assaulting a toddler, according to CNN affiliate reports.

Chester Arthur Stiles, 38, now faces a maximum sentence of life in prison. He was found guilty of lewdness with a child, sexual assault of a minor, attempted sexual assault of a minor, and several related charges. According to KLAS, Stiles displayed no visible reaction as the verdict was announced. Sentencing has been scheduled for May 8.

The case triggered a nationwide manhunt in 2007 after the videotape first surfaced, sparking an intensive search to identify and locate the young victim.

During the trial, jurors were shown the videotape, though the presiding judge barred courtroom spectators from viewing it—a screen was erected to shield the jury box from public view, according to Michael Sommermeyer, spokesman for the Clark County, Nevada courts. Select members of the media were permitted to view the footage as well; however, the judge restricted broader access out of concern that visible reactions from reporters or onlookers might influence the jury's deliberations.

The charges also encompassed a second girl whom Stiles was accused of sexually assaulting on video.

The tape had been turned over to authorities in September 2007 by a man who claimed to have discovered it in the desert five months earlier. Upon reviewing the footage, investigators found disturbing images of a young girl being sexually assaulted. After initial efforts to identify the child proved unsuccessful, authorities enlisted media assistance and released her photograph publicly—prompting a case that captured national attention. The girl was ultimately located in October 2007.

An attorney representing the girl's mother confirmed that the child was 7 years old, safe, and in good health. The assault had occurred before her third birthday, while she was under the care of a babysitter hired by her mother, who had no knowledge that her daughter had been victimized. Once the girl was identified and found, authorities requested that CNN and other news outlets cease circulating her photograph. In a subsequent appearance on "The Dr. Phil Show," the girl's mother stated that her daughter retained no memory of the assault.

Stiles, a resident of Pahrump, Nevada, was apprehended during a routine traffic stop in October 2007. Police reported that they initially pulled over his vehicle due to a missing license plate, growing suspicious when Stiles produced an expired California driver's license bearing a photo that did not match his appearance. He ultimately acknowledged his identity and confirmed that he was the subject of the ongoing search, authorities said.

Darrin Tuck, the man who submitted the videotape to authorities, faced criminal charges of his own due to the delay in reporting it—during which he allegedly showed the footage to other individuals. In April, a judge sentenced Tuck to a one-year suspended sentence and three years of probation after he pleaded guilty to conspiracy to obstruct a public officer, the Las Vegas Review-Journal reported. He had originally faced a felony charge of possessing child pornography.
